correctness.rationale: A general-position set in a complete multipartite graph is either in one part or uses at most one vertex per part; this gives the source coefficient formula. For \(t\ge4\), exact polynomial identities show strictly positive adjacent log-concavity defects at k=1..6, with all larger k inherited from the strict binomial sequence. All rational positivity lists have positive coefficients after shifting t by four or six. Standard-library exact polynomial algebra reproduced each identity. At \(t=2\) and \(t=3\) explicit negative defects -50 and -240 respectively disprove log-concavity; their explicit coefficient sequences are unimodal. A separate adjacency/geodesic enumerator matched the polynomial for every subset on 10- and 15-vertex graphs. No finite sample is used to infer the infinite result.

The foundational 2024 article and indexed nearby records do not give a theorem implying this sharp cutoff. Priority is provisional, not a claim of globally exhaustive absence.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating article gives a general part-size<=4 theorem, explicitly leaves precise parameter-pair classification for future work, and exhibits the isolated (size five, two parts) failure. The present theorem resolves the entire first missing five-vertex-part line, with an exact sharp threshold at four parts and a second exceptional failure at a different coefficient index. This is a motivated infinite-parametric shape classification rather than a routine restatement of the known coefficient formula.
